rows.my_view: Base case $8.00 with a bear $3.50 and bull $27.50, and watchlist implies the price is ahead of fair value.
rows.committee: Expensive at 27.6x sales on $53M revenue and ~20% above the owner's own $8 base case, so today's price already pays for a platform the financials do not yet contain.

rows.my_view: Revenue is real but must prove quality against lumpy, episodic government demand.
rows.committee: Agree — the +381% quarter is loud but the path whipsaws violently ($4.6M to $17.8M to $7.3M to $40.7M) and ships near-margin-free with no disclosed funded backlog.

rows.my_view: Margins must expand materially from current levels — this is the crux of the thesis.
rows.committee: Agree this is the crux, with one reservation: the 3% may be structural or early-lot pricing, and the $52M net-loss-vs-cash gap suggests part is working-capital build the data can't yet separate.

rows.my_view: The Army qualification is an emerging structural advantage if the selection becomes funded.
rows.committee: The China-free qualification barrier is a genuine seed, but it is unproven, rests on a possibly-unfunded selection, and the 3% gross margin is the direct refutation of pricing power today.

rows.my_view: Treat the product family as optionality and watch for dilution without per-share value.
rows.committee: The 'optionality' is being funded by active cash burn and dilution now — a paid position, not a free option — with shares up from 48M to 152M in four years.

rows.my_view: Dilution and low margin before the economics prove out.
rows.committee: Same risks, but sharper: Q1 burned $91.3M FCF — nearly all of last year's $95.8M — leaving ~1.4 quarters of runway, so a raise is near-imminent, not distant.

rows.my_view: Mistaking acquisition breadth for a coherent platform.
rows.committee: The runway was read at the smoother TTM pace, missing the quarterly burn detonation, and the entry-price problem — a stock that already ran to $18.78 and fell 49% with the base case below current price.

rows.my_view: Follow-on Army funding and broadening orders.
rows.committee: Gross margin sustained above 25% for two consecutive quarters alongside disclosure of a firm, funded multi-year SRR contract — the one combination that flips this to Open.

confidence.label: High
confidence.why: The owner pre-registered the exact doubts — margin quality, funded-versus-objective, dilution — that the run independently confirmed, leaving only degree, not direction, in dispute.

final_verdict: The watchlist is earned: an asymmetric, unbuilt business priced above its own base case with a near-forced dilution clock, waiting on margin proof and a funded contract.
